questions.question: Describe suiphide group of minerals with example / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• The sulphide group of minerals is predominantly metallic in character, and many of these
  • minerals are opaque. Their hardness ranges from about 1 to 6 or more, as in the case of
  • pyrite. Definition-(1 mark). A good example of a sulphide mineral is galena (PbS), the
  • most important lead -bearing mineral in the Earth's crust. Galena is also one of the most
  • common sulphide minerals and serves as the primary source of lead. -Example (1 mark)

questions.question: Describe how streak offer a more dependable clue to mineral identity than surface colour. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• The color of powder of a mineral as obtained by scratching the surface of the mineral with
  • a knife or file, if the mineral is not too hard, by rubbing it on an unglazed porcelain surface,
  • is called the streak. Definition- (2 marks). The streak is often very important quality in
  • distinguishing minerals. Streak is an independent property while compared to color. For
  • example- hematite and magnetite are black in color, while their streak cherry red and black
  • in color. - Explanation (4 marks). Example (2 marks)

questions.question: Discuss the role of halides in the chemical industry. / [CO6]
questions.solution_html:
• Halides find their greatest use in the production of sodium compounds and chlorine. Sylvite
  • and other potassium salts are used in fertilizers, as well as in the manufacture of dyes and
  • soaps. Definition with examples - (3.5 marks). Large quantities of fluorite are used in
  • metallurgical operations as a flux. Halides are also essential for making plastics such as
  • polyvinyl chloride (PVC) and synthetic rubber. In electronics, halides play an important
  • role in the production of semiconductors and are used in processes like etching and metal
  • coating. They also help control electrochemical reactions and prevent corrosion in various
  • industries. – Uses-(4.5 marks).
